newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Mexico's Zedillo reaffirms Latin American ties.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo reaffirms Latin American ties.

text.p: Visiting Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said Wednesday that Mexico wants to bolster relations with other nations in Latin America, which in recent years have been outshone by links with the developed world.

"Things like the North American Free Trade Agreement...and our membership to APEC have left the sensation that Mexico was not interested or was not looking to the south or that it had abandoned its Latin American orientation," Zedillo told a news conference held with Argentine President Carlos Menem.

"What has been of most interest to me in this trip has been to provide evidence that Mexico and its government are extremely interested in developing a new relation with Argentina, and certainly with other brother countries of Latin America," he said.
Apart from being a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) along with the United States and Canada, Mexico is also part of the Asia Pacific Economic Forum (APEC).
Zedillo invited Argentina Tuesday to be Mexico's main ally in reaching a trade agreement with South America's Mercosur customs union, which also groups Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.

He said Wednesday he did not expect Mexico's NAFTA partners to be concerned about the country's overtures to Mercosur, and pointed out that Mexico had received no comments about similar talks with the European Union.

"There have not been any questions by the United States government over our starting these conversations with the European Union," he said. Rules of origin clauses avoid clashes between trade agreements, he said.
In a joint-declaration, Zedillo and Menem reaffirmed their commitment to forging an Americas-wide free trade area.

The declaration also reaffirmed Mexico's support for Argentina in its territorial dispute with Britain over the Falkland Islands and criticized the U.S. attempt to clamp down on investment in Cuba through the Helms Burton Law.

Zedillo arrived in Buenos Aires Tuesday accompanied by 40 businessmen in his first visit to a Mercosur country since taking ofice in 1994. He is due to leave Argentina Thursday, after signing an investment protection treaty.
